title: The Protocol of the Rust Belt
premise: Freya Eriksen has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's abandoned seed vault, recording daily logs for a colony that stopped listening long ago. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the anomaly originated from the vault itself — a dormant protocol buried in her own memory implants, seeded there before she was hired. Accompanied by Caspian Voss, a defected relay technician who arrives seeking her, Freya must cross dead space to reach the outer relay and decide whether to broadcast the truth about the colony's deliberate abandonment or preserve the comforting lie that kept humanity's last outposts loyal. At the relay, she chooses truth — transmitting everything, including her own complicity — as the flickering gravity finally stills and the colonies, awake at last, begin to answer.
about_author: Yara Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data in northern Scandinavia. Her fiction blends quiet domestic isolation with vast, indifferent systems, and 'The Protocol of the Rust Belt' is her third novel.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. During her 4,000th daily log entry, gravity across the entire system stutters for nine seconds; seeds drift from their racks like snow. She records it with shaking hands, realizing no one else may have noticed. Emotional beat: eerie wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Freya's POV. Eleven years of solitary routine: checking seals, rationing power, speaking aloud to keep sane. We learn the colony ships went silent three years ago and she logs anyway. Emotional beat: devotion as both purpose and prison.

chapters.title: A Light on the Ice
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. A single shuttle breaches dead space toward the vault — impossible, since all traffic was recalled years ago. Caspian Voss lands uninvited, claiming he followed the nine-second anomaly's signature. Emotional beat: suspicion sharpened by desperate hope.

chapters.title: Two Sets of Footprints
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Freya and Caspian circle each other through the vault's frozen corridors; he knows things about the relay network she doesn't, she knows the vault's rhythms he can't fake. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming over shared coffee and mutual lies.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Auditing the vault after the anomaly, Freya finds data packets hidden inside seed-genome files — addressed to her implant ID. Someone planned this before she was ever hired. Emotional beat: the ground of identity giving way.

chapters.title: The Defector's Confession
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. He admits he deserted the relay corps after discovering the colony silence wasn't an accident — it was ordered, and covered by the same protocol now waking in Freya's head. Emotional beat: guilt offered like a wound.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Blindness
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She refuses to believe the administration betrayed the colonies; her whole life was built on serving them. She nearly ejects Caspian. Emotional beat: love of duty at war with emerging doubt.

chapters.title: The Vault Wakes
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. The vault's dormant systems activate, projecting a star map: a route to the outer relay through dead space, timed against a second gravity event. The protocol wants them to go. Emotional beat: being moved like pieces on a board.

chapters.title: Departure Without Permission
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She locks the vault, leaves her final caretaker log unfinished mid-sentence, and boards Caspian's shuttle. The act feels like betrayal and freedom at once. Emotional beat: grief disguised as resolve.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Dead Air
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The crossing: radiation ghosts, failing comms, and long silences where they trade truths instead of instruments. First real intimacy. Emotional beat: two lonely people learning each other's frequencies.

chapters.title: The Colony That Wasn't Lost
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. They pass the derelict colony ship Meridian — not destroyed, but deliberately powered down with everyone aboard in unscheduled cryo. Evidence of the cover-up, physical and terrible. Emotional beat: horror rendered intimate by names on crew manifests.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Her implants begin broadcasting fragments she never recorded — memories that aren't hers, including a woman's voice calling her by another name. The protocol is rewriting her. Emotional beat: selfhood dissolving at the edges.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the outer relay station, rusted and half-alive, and find it manned: Administrator Sorel, who claims to be its last honest servant. His welcome is warm; his locks are armed. Emotional beat: relief shadowed by wrongness.

chapters.title: Sorel's Version of Events
chapters.summary: Sorel's POV. He tells them the colonies failed naturally and the silence spared billions from panic; the protocol exists to prevent truth from killing hope. He offers Freya restoration, home, erasure of doubt. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Cold Room
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Alone in the relay's archive, Freya finds the original orders — signed by someone whose name matches the voice in her implanted memories. She understands she was built for this choice. Emotional beat: fury transmuting into clarity.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Close Range
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. Sorel moves to seize the shuttle and wipe them both; Caspian sabotages the relay's uplink to buy time and is captured. He sends Freya one message: run, or finish it. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony.

chapters.title: What Love Cannot Protect
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya could escape with the evidence and live; broadcasting means triggering the second gravity event, which may kill the sleepers aboard Meridian. Truth versus every life she might save by lying. Emotional beat: the loneliest decision of her life.

chapters.title: The Second Flicker
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The countdown begins. Freya fights through the relay's defenses, frees Caspian, and reaches the transmitter as gravity begins to stutter again — the protocol forcing her hand. Emotional beat: momentum beyond hesitation.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She transmits everything: the orders, the Meridian, her own engineered memory, Sorel's complicity — and then, unprompted, adds eleven years of caretaker logs, the human record no protocol anticipated. Emotional beat: release, terrifying and total.

chapters.title: Gravity Holds
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. The nine seconds pass; the system steadies. Across dead space, faint responses begin arriving — colony ships waking, voices returning one by one. Sorel surrenders the relay rather than kill the messenger twice. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving joy.

chapters.title: Answers Arriving Slowly
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Weeks later, rescue ships approach Meridian; some sleepers wake, some don't, and Freya reads every name aloud into the record. Caspian stays. The vault will need a new caretaker — perhaps two. Emotional beat: mourning braided with beginning.

chapters.title: The Protocol of the Rust Belt
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, final log. Back at the vault, she records entry 4,001: not a report to absent masters, but a letter to whoever comes next. The rust belt hums with returning traffic. She signs off with her real name. Emotional beat: wholeness reclaimed.
